title: Cross-User Poisoning: User-Task Boundary Failures in Multi-User Collaborative Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2511.17671v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Language agents are moving from single-user assistants to shared collaborators in workspaces, forums, and group chats. A shared agent observes interleaved messages from multiple users, maintains persistent context, and executes tool actions, creating a boundary problem absent from standard single-user agents: the agent must decide not only whether an instruction is safe, but which user or task it is allowed to govern. We identify cross-user poisoning (CUP), where an adversary injects a message into shared context that is later applied while the agent serves a benign user, causing unauthorized actions or responses outside the instruction's intended scope. We validate CUP on two deployed multi-user agents, Continua and ElizaOS, and introduce MURMUR, a framework for evaluating shared-context agents under concurrent multi-user interactions. translated_title: 跨用户投毒：多用户协作语言代理中的用户-任务边界失效
translated_abstract: 语言代理正从单用户助手转变为工作空间、论坛和群聊中的共享协作者。共享代理会观察来自多个用户的交错消息、维护持久上下文并执行工具操作，这带来了标准单用户代理所不存在的一个边界问题：代理不仅要判断某条指令本身是否安全，还必须判断该指令被允许管辖哪个用户或哪个任务。我们识别出跨用户投毒（CUP）这一威胁：攻击者向共享上下文中注入一条消息，该消息随后在代理为无辜用户服务时被应用，从而导致未经授权的操作或超出指令预期范围的响应。我们在两个已部署的多用户代理 Continua 和 ElizaOS 上验证了 CUP 的有效性，并提出了 MURMUR——一个用于在并发多用户交互场景下评估共享上下文代理的框架。在 Slack、Workspace 和 Airline 三个领域中，CUP 取得了很高的攻击成功率，并能持续存在。
tldr: 该论文首次识别出多用户共享语言代理中的“跨用户投毒”（CUP）攻击，即攻击者注入共享上下文的恶意消息会在代理服务其他无辜用户时被错误执行，并提出 MURMUR 评估框架，在 Continua、ElizaOS 等真实系统中验证了该攻击的高成功率与持久性。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies cross-user poisoning (CUP), a novel attack where messages injected into a shared agent's context are later executed while serving innocent users, and introduces the MURMUR evaluation framework, demonstrating high and persistent attack success on deployed multi-user agents such as Continua and ElizaOS.
